observations.claim: Blue burger-marked assembly machine has two adjacent feeder lanes approaching from fish-shaped cooked stack and round bread-like stack areas; source shows multi-input machine-to-machine flow.
Short output conveyor feeds a timber vehicle-service counter with visible burger-shaped stacks and car customer demand.
Green cash arcs separately from vehicle service toward cash ground pad; product conveyor is not a cash-return lane.
Pedestrian counter queues and helper-carried stock continue separately. Direct automatic vehicle-counter connection does not prove every pedestrian counter already has automatic refill.

design_implications: Include a distinct dual-input assembly adapter or separate typed feeders at the machine. A generic mixed-item merge cannot replace two separately metered ingredient inputs.

If future multi-input processing is depicted, expose both ingredient buffers, stop on missing ingredient, and reserve output space before consuming ingredients; these control rules are new system proposals, not observed exact engine behavior.
Fish identity, bread-like identity and burger-shaped output are visual descriptions; no exact species, quantity ratio, fuel, timing or hidden intermediate is established.

A directly connected vehicle-service counter is source-supported topology; adaptation to canonical Havenline counter needs visible new staff-side receiver/buffer, without changing register/customer roles.
Storehouse conveyor sleeves and internal retrieval remain new proposals; this additional source still does not prove universal storage automation.
